I’ve moved the compatibility logic out of the heap core. I’m adjusting the tests to exercise those legacy names through the compatibility interface explicitly, which makes the layering clearer and keeps the modern-path tests separate.

The compatibility split is done. I’m rebuilding with lint again to make sure the new interface-based layering is clean and that removing those adapter methods from `MinHeap` didn’t leave any dead assumptions behind.

Refactored the API layering so the modern heap surface and the compatibility surface are no longer mixed together. [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:1) now only implements the canonical `IntHeap` operations plus the compatibility interface, while all deprecated names live as default methods in [LegacyMinHeapApi.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/LegacyMinHeapApi.java:1). That keeps the public class smaller and makes the legacy behavior explicit instead of scattering deprecated wrappers through the implementation.

I also simplified [IntBinaryHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/IntBinaryHeap.java:4) by removing adapter-only methods that the modern heap core no longer needs. The test suite in [MinHeapTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeapTest.java:45) now exercises legacy behavior through `LegacyMinHeapApi` directly, while the shared removal helper was generalized to `IntHeap` so both layers use the same assertions cleanly.
